title: Does Your ViT Still Need U-Net for Segmentation? (EoSeg)
mechanism: Encoder-only query segmenter for small medical sets: queries refined through the last 3 DINOv2-L blocks, a learned gate fuses per-block predictions, 2 queries per class.
adaptation: Use as the small-data recipe for the EoMT arm: 2 queries per class (48), block-fusion gate, AdamW 5e-4 with layer decay, about 12k steps at batch 8 on 478 cells; add 1024 input and full-res head for cracks; judge on inactive and E1, not strict crack IoU.
min_experiment: Fold into EoMT arm as variant: EoMT-L vs EoMT-L + EoSeg block fusion + 2 queries/class, 5-fold CV; metric inactive IoU and mIoU_rob; kill the variant if it does not beat plain EoMT by > 0.01 mIoU_rob fold-paired.
evidence: R: Synapse (18 train volumes) 85.50 DSC vs TransUNet 77.48, SwinUNet 79.13; ablation 82.40 linear head -> 83.70 query masks -> 84.34 multi-level -> 84.78 fusion -> 85.50 two queries per class; DINOv2-L 81.86 vs DINOv3-L 81.60; GlaS Dice 93.27 (5-fold). No nnU-Net comparison. Code stated as github.com/Retinal-Research/EoSeg (not opened).
